# Person

A person involved in the estate. Schema.org name alignment. Any Unicode script. Supports CJK phonetic readings, chieftaincy titles, clan/lineage identifiers, dual legal personalities, and tax residency across multiple jurisdictions

Source: [`v3/person.json`](../../v3/person.json)

Schema `$id`: `https://openinherit.org/v3/person.json`

## Properties

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` (uuid) | yes | Unique identifier for this person within the INHERIT document. Must be referenced consistently across all entities |
| `givenName` | `string` | yes | The person's given (first) name. For cultures where given name follows family name (e.g. Japanese, Chinese), this is still the given name — display ordering is a presentation concern |
| `familyName` | `string` | | The person's family name (surname). Some cultures do not use family names — Tamil, Icelandic patronymic, and mononymous naming conventions are all valid without this field |
| `additionalName` | `string` | | Middle name(s) or additional given names. Multiple middle names should be space-separated |
| `preferredName` | `string` | | Name the person prefers to be called. May differ from legal name — use this for correspondence and display where appropriate |
| `phoneticReading` | `object` | | Phonetic reading of the person's name. Essential for CJK names to ensure correct pronunciation by non-native speakers and systems |
| `titles` | array of `object` | | Formal titles held by this person. Multiple titles are common — a person may hold academic, professional, and traditional titles simultaneously |
| `clanOrLineage` | `string` | | Clan, tribe, lineage, or gotra affiliation. In some legal systems (Hindu, customary African), this determines inheritance rights and succession order |
| `dateOfBirth` | `string` (date) | | The person's date of birth in ISO 8601 format. Used to determine age-dependent inheritance rights and guardianship requirements |
| `dateOfDeath` | `string` (date) | | The person's date of death in ISO 8601 format, if deceased. Relevant for determining predecease rules, commorientes, and survivorship |
| `gender` | one of `male`, `female`, `non_binary`, `other`, `prefer_not_to_say`, `unknown` | | The person's gender. Optional, but required where inheritance rules are gender-dependent (e.g. Islamic faraid, Hindu succession) |
| `domicile` | [Jurisdiction](common/jurisdiction.md) | | The person's legal domicile. Domicile — not nationality or residence — determines which succession law governs moveable property |
| `roles` | array of one of `testator`, `beneficiary`, `executor`, `guardian`, `trustee`, `witness`, `attorney`, `proxy`, `protector`, `enforcer` | yes | The roles this person plays in the estate. A person may hold multiple roles simultaneously (e.g. beneficiary and executor) |
| `contact` | `object` | | Contact details for this person. All fields are optional — some parties may have no known contact information |
| `preferredChannel` | one of `email`, `phone`, `post`, `in_person`, `video_call`, `messaging` | | This person's preferred communication channel. Helps executors and professionals contact the right people in the right way |
| `identifiers` | array of [Identifier](common/identifier.md) | | External identifiers for this person — passport numbers, national ID, tax reference numbers, etc. Used for probate applications and cross-border identification |
| `ritualName` | `object` | | The person's name within a religious naming tradition. Required for religious court filings, halachic documents, and Shariah proceedings |
| `legalPersonalities` | array of `object` | | Legal personalities this person holds across different legal systems. A single person may have distinct legal identities under statutory, customary, and religious law simultaneously |
| `taxResidency` | array of `object` | | Tax residency declarations for one or more jurisdictions. A person may be simultaneously tax-resident in multiple countries, triggering reporting obligations under FATCA, CRS, and bilateral treaties |
| `sharedWithCompanion` | `boolean` | | Whether this person record is shared with the companion estate. When true, changes sync between linked estates |
| `language` | `string` | | BCP 47 language tag for the person's preferred language. Used for correspondence and document generation |
| `notes` | `string` | | Free-text notes about this person. Use for anything not captured by structured fields — health conditions, access requirements, or context for professionals |
| `fieldProvenance` | array of [FieldProvenance](common/field-provenance.md) | | Per-field provenance records — how each field's value was obtained |
| `comments` | array of `object` | | Discussion comments on this entity |
| `accessibilityNeeds` | `object` | | Accessibility requirements for communicating with and providing services to this person |
| `sameAs` | array of `string` (uri) | | URIs identifying this entity elsewhere (schema.org sameAs). e.g. Wikidata, LinkedIn, DBpedia |
| `provenance` | [Provenance](common/provenance.md) | | Consolidated provenance metadata — how this entity was created, by whom, and whether a human has verified it |
| `jurisdictionRoles` | array of `object` | | Extension-specific roles that the core roles enum cannot cover — e.g. faraid_heir, karta, okpara |
| `posthumousAiConsent` | `object` | | The person's wishes regarding posthumous AI recreation of their likeness or identity. Typically set on the testator and possibly their spouse |
| `identity` | `object` | | Canonical identity for cross-document person matching. The fingerprint is deterministic: same inputs always produce the same key |
| `religion` | `object` | | The person's religious affiliation as a legal status. In jurisdictions where religion determines succession law (Singapore AMLA, Malaysian faraid, Israeli rabbinical courts), this is a jurisdictional switch, not a personal belief declaration |

Also accepts properties whose names match `^x-inherit-[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,54}$`.
